html:
President of the Philippines from 1965 to 1986, who ruled under martial law for most of the 1970s and stole billions of dollars before he was driven out.

A lawyer and politician from Ilocos Norte, Marcos won the presidency in 1965 and became the first to be re-elected, in 1969. Barred from a third term, he declared martial law in 1972, closed Congress and the press, and jailed opponents. Thousands were tortured or killed. As a Cold War ally of the United States he kept American support.

He and his wife Imelda built showy projects and handed whole industries to friends, while the foreign debt soared. In 1983 the opposition leader Ninoy Aquino was shot dead at Manila airport on his return from exile. Anger spread.

Marcos called a snap election in 1986 against Aquino's widow, Corazon Aquino, and claimed a win through fraud. The People Power Revolution followed, and he fled to Hawaii, where he died in 1989. His son became president in 2022.
sum: President of the Philippines from 1965 to 1986, who ruled under martial law for most of the 1970s and stole billions of dollars before he was driven out.
